metadata.note: The Birmingham and Northwestern Railway, Jackson - Dyersburg, west Tennessee (48.473 mi). Despite the name it never reached Alabama. One feature: the B&NW itself, drawn 1912-1919 [OPEN]. The Gulf, Mobile and Northern (lease 1927) and Gulf, Mobile and Ohio (1940) eras are deliberately NOT drawn: no passenger train under either operator has been sourced, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide index lists the branch's stations in no timetable.
not_yet_sourced: bnw-jackson-dyersburg END YEAR [OPEN]: 1919 is the last dated passenger train found (USRA notice, Dec 1919, trains 1 and 4 discontinued as a temporary coal-strike cut). Passenger engine and coach still owned Aug 1922. Service very probably continued to some unknown date before the GM&N lease of Mar 1927; whether the Dec 1919 cut was restored is unknown. A 1920s Official Guide, Tennessee RR & Public Utilities Commission discontinuance order or a Jackson Sun / Dyersburg State Gazette 'last train' item would settle it.
Whether the Gulf, Mobile and Northern (1927-1940) or Gulf, Mobile and Ohio (1940-) ran any passenger train (perhaps a motor car) on the branch: plausible, unsourced, so not drawn.
Headway (360 min) and avg_speed_kmh (35) are estimates.
Sites of the B&NW passenger stations at Jackson and Dyersburg.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru and overpass-api.de; the mirrors were throttling, so the routing graph was built from corridor queries rather than whole degree tiles), traced with opstrace.py. Probed old_railway_operator over the corridor: the road is tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O with note:old_railway_operator='GM&N (Birmingham and Northwestern)'; no way uses B&NW or Birmingham and Northwestern in old_railway_operator itself. opstrace's Operator match was extended in the tracing script to read note:old_railway_operator. OpenHistoricalMap also carries the line (operator 'Birmingham and Northwestern Railroad', ways 201838160-201838162) but was not needed: the trace is identical without it.

properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no running time was found for this short steam branch (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass, traced with opstrace.py: the ways whose note:old_railway_operator reads 'GM&N (Birmingham and Northwestern)' (old_railway_operator=GM&O) - active/abandoned track out of Jackson (ways 19552183, 169236522, 429703200-429703216) and the 60.8 km razed grade way 165229807 to Dyersburg, ending on the B&NW-noted spur 19450823.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 48.6 mi drawn against 48.473 mi documented (ICC valuation; Fowler 48.5). Every mile of the line runs on OSM ways noted as the Birmingham and Northwestern (old_railway_operator=GM&O, note:old_railway_operator='GM&N (Birmingham and Northwestern)'); none rides Illinois Central, L&N, Southern or M&O/GM&N main-line track. Waypoint fit: Bells 0.7 km, Alamo 0.5 km, Crockett Mills 0.1 km, Friendship 0.6 km, Tigrett 0.1 km from the line (town-centre geocodes, not depot sites). Jackson end: drawn to the east end of the B&NW-noted abandoned spur (way 19552183, about 35.614 N, 88.825 W, west of downtown); the exact site of the B&NW's Jackson passenger station is not established and the last few hundred metres to it, if any, are not drawn. Dyersburg end: the B&NW-noted spur (way 19450823) on the west side of town short of the IC main; the B&NW station site is likewise not established. ALIGNMENT: the 1912 alignment is believed to be the one drawn (the OSM grade is the only one recorded for this road and no realignment is mentioned in the research), but the Jackson approach is today's West Tennessee Railroad-era track and was not checked against a 1912-20 map.

segments.note: Birmingham and Northwestern Railway, built 1911-12 by the Jackson Construction Co. (president Isaac B. Tigrett). Jackson - Tigrett (38 mi) opened Apr 20, 1912 and Tigrett - Dyersburg (11 mi) June 16, 1912; Lemly: 'passenger service was offered from the start'. Steam throughout (no Rule 5 issue). Stations (Fowler): Jackson, Experiment Station, White Oak, Pearson, Roberts, Brittain, Bells, Alamo, Nichols, Crockett Mills, Maury Junction, Friendship, Tigrett, Carpenter, Parkers, Bishop, Dyersburg. Year to June 30, 1916: 4 locomotives, 5 passenger cars (Lemly). 1918-20 under USRA federal control grouped with the NC&StL; that did not change who ran the trains. [OPEN] END: 1919 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. The latest dated passenger evidence is a U.S. Railroad Administration notice (News Scimitar, Memphis, Dec 6, 1919) discontinuing B&NW trains Nos. 1 and 4 Jackson - Dyersburg from Dec 9, 1919 as a temporary coal-strike measure; train numbers imply at least two pairs, so some service probably remained, and restoration was not found. Service very probably continued: a passenger engine and coach were damaged in the Jackson shop fire of Aug 11, 1922 (North Mississippi Herald, Aug 18, 1922) - equipment, not a timetable. No dated train after 1919 has been found, and the B&NW ran the line until the Gulf, Mobile and Northern took it over under lease in Mar 1927, so the true end lies at an unknown date between Dec 1919 and 1927 (or later, under GM&N/GM&O, which is not drawn). Do not extend without evidence. Headway 360 min is an estimate (roughly two trains each way a day, inferred from train numbers 1 and 4), not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1912 opening (Jackson-Tigrett Apr 20, through to Dyersburg June 16, 1912; 'passenger service was offered from the start') from Lemly; 1919 end is the last dated passenger train found (USRA notice discontinuing B&NW trains Nos. 1 and 4 Jackson-Dyersburg eff. Dec 9, 1919, News Scimitar, Memphis, Dec 6, 1919, p.15). Headway and speed not sourced.
